newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks mixed in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks mixed in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened higher then eased on Wednesday morning, pulled down by renewed profit-taking in the finance sector despite the jump in the Dow overnight and a rebound in property share prices, brokers said.
"The market doesn't look very good," said Franco Tong, in institutional sales at New China Hong Kong. "The Dow was up but we are headed down."
The Hang Seng Index was trading 16 points, or 0.11 percent, lower at 14,808 on turnover of HK$2.52 billion.
Overnight, the Dow industrials rose 103.82 points, or 1.32 percent, to 7,962.31.
Properties outperformed the market, rebounding after a recent heavy sell-off.
But brokers were cautious on the sector after comments by Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa.
"The overhang of Tung's property proposals will continue until we see a further fall in property prices," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.
"The risk to the market is that Mr Tung will have some medium to long-term plan to curb speculation and bring down residential property prices, especially luxury residential (units)."
Cheung Kong led the property sector, adding HK$2.00 to HK$75.00.
Further profit-taking in the finance sector and in China-controlled red chips was likely, brokers said.
HSBC dipped to a low of HK$243.00 before rising to HK$245.00, up HK$1.00. Hang Seng Bank was HK$0.50 lower at HK$106.00.
"I think we are going to see a quiet market in coming days," said Cheung. "The speculators won't be back in this market soon."
A series of measures taken by Beijing authorities has cooled speculation in Shanghai and Shenzhen market, and this had a knock-on effect on Hong Kong.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index of 32 red chips lagged the market, dipping 0.52 percent to 3,278.89. China Resources shed HK$0.40 to HK$33.70.
